ground_truth.description: The suppression check relies on semantic/vector search (`search(query="stage1_flag_suppression", ...)`) to locate a specific task's suppression record. Vector search returns only a bounded top-k ranked by similarity, so when suppression records exist for many tasks (or the corpus is large), the record for the target task_id may not appear in the results at all. The check then concludes 'no suppression in effect' and emits the flag — a false negative that exactly matches the flagged symptom (review passed but escalation_created). A deterministic metadata lookup (e.g. get_memories_by_metadata / count_memories_by_metadata filtered on kind+task_id) is required.

The search query string is the generic literal "stage1_flag_suppression" and does not include the target task_id, so records for all other tasks compete for the limited top-k slots and can crowd out the relevant task's record, again causing the target's suppression to be missed.

The validity test requires `metadata.task_id == <N>` as an integer, but metadata persisted through Mem0 may store the task_id as a string; a strict integer equality check would then reject a genuine suppression record and fall through to emitting the flag (false negative). The comparison should be type-normalized.

provenance.runs_db_query: SELECT task_id, project_id, outcome, review_cycles, verify_attempts FROM task_results WHERE review_cycles >= 1, cross-referenced with events (escalation_created, merge_finalized) -- see mining.mine_fn_candidates.
